uses.quote: If you have been given permission to use GenAI, it can be most helpful in the planning stages of your work.
You can also ask GenAI for feedback on what you've written, and the more specific you can be the better.
You can cut and paste a section of open access text into Copilot and ask for a summary to help you understand the original.

uses.quote: AI tools such as Adobe’s Firefly can also generate images and audio which might serve as starting points for projects.
you can copy word-for-word, without referencing, sentence fragments that don’t contain facts. These should be no more than 5-8 words long, and you should limit the amount of these
uses.anchor: Consider how much text to use

uses.quote: You must not directly copy larger chunks of text or images that have been produced for you by AI without attributing the source
Tools with enhanced AI functionality like Grammarly or paraphrasing applications offer substantial text rewrites which if copied and pasted directly into your work would count as academic misconduct.
Use LEAs to point out but not automatically correct poor grammar and writing.
Any use of translation tools in assessed work must be clearly acknowledged and referenced.
GenAI can invent facts that seem plausible (‘hallucinations’), therefore you must check everything it says with a reputable source
